title: Feasibility of Real-Time Neural Decoding During AM-tACS in a Bi-Directional BCI in Chronic Stroke Survivors
summary:
Stroke can damage the parts of the brain that control movement, often leaving people with a weak or poorly functioning hand. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) can help assisting their motor training: they pick up brain signals when a person imagines a movement and use them to control a device, such as a robotic hand exoskeleton that opens and closes the hand. At the same time, non-invasive brain stimulation, in which a very weak electrical current is applied through the scalp to influence brain activity, can support motor recovery.
This study tests whether these two approaches can be combined as a novel strategy to support motor training after stroke. The combination has already been tested in healthy volunteers. Now we want to test whether it also works in people who had a stroke more than one year ago, and whether it is feasible in clinical practice. At this stage, we are not testing whether the approach improves movement or recovery. We want to find out whether brain signals can still be recorded reliably while stimulation is switched on, and whether the stimulation changes brain activity. If the approach proves technically feasible and well tolerated, future studies will investigate its clinical efficacy when integrated into long-term training.
conditions: Chronic Stroke Survivors with lasting neurological deficits (ICD-10-GM-169.-)

interventions.name: This study investigates the feasibility of a novel paradigm that combines a brain-controlled exoskeleton with non-invasive brain stimulation in chronic stroke survivors. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
⁠•⁠ Reliable performance of the motor imagery task
⁠•⁠ Good fit of the robotic exoskeleton
Exclusion criteria:
•⁠ ⁠Other neurological or psychiatric conditions 
•⁠ ⁠Epilepsy or a history of seizures (including in the family)
•⁠ ⁠Pregnancy
•⁠ ⁠Alcohol or drug abuse
•⁠ ⁠Metallic or magnetic implants or other contraindications for MRI scans
